thread:
incident-bot: Pager: hosted-runtime kv-cache OOMs observed in eu-west-1. Alerting oncall. severity: high :rotating_light:

mike: seeing repeated OOMs on host runtime-3, kv-cache size spiking to >40GB per process, nodes hitting OOM kill. customer error bursts around long prompt completions.

sophie: which customers? any public-facing latency spikes? :eyes:

mike: a handful of PLG customers hitting long conversation histories. internal dashboards show continuous-batching window growth correlating with long prompts + prefix caching.

raj: I can join. I suspect the prefetch controller is aggressively populating KV for long sessions. we hit the perf cliff where batching + prefetch amplifies context.

emily: adding context: autoscaler didn't trigger more nodes because memory drain was sudden, not CPU. eviction pressure triggered cascade.

oncall-sre: oncall here. assign to eng-runtime for immediate mitigation. cc @eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: on it. quick mitigation options: 1) disable KV_PREFETCH for hosted runtime in eu-west-1 2) reduce continuous batching window (BATCH_WINDOW_MS -> 25) 3) enforce per-session max_kv_tokens=4096.

mike: disabling prefetch sounds fastest. how do we flip that at scale?

eng-runtime: we have a dynamic config layer. plan: set runtime.dynamic.kv_prefetch.enabled=false for eu-west-1 via console API, then restart a subset of runtime pods to pick up config. patch + rollout can be ~45s for control-plane propagation.

raj: also prepare a hotfix to reduce batch max tokens to 512 and drop continuous-batch depth to 1 for this region. that'll lower memory amplification.

emily: customer impact assessment: initial spike caused ~32% of in-flight requests to fail with 500 memory errors for ~6 minutes. post-spike errors still ~2-3%. Affected customers have been contacted via support with incident references.

mike: rolling config now: calling console API.

eng-runtime: runbook command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","key":"runtime.dynamic.kv_prefetch.enabled","value":"false"}'
```

raj: issuing patch to batching config too: 
```
kubectl -n runtime patch cm batching-config -p '{"data":{"BATCH_MAX_TOKENS":"512","CONT_BATCH_DEPTH":"1"}}'
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/runtime-eu-west-1
```

mike: patch accepted by control plane. applying rollout to canary subset (20%). will monitor OOM rate.

sophie: logs show immediate drop in kv-cache growth for canary instances—nice. OOM events reduced on those nodes within 90s.

oncall-sre: escalate to platform pager duty: ask infra to temporarily scale up swap-backed nodes if OOMs continue. prepping capacity.

eng-runtime: canary looks good. proceeding with region-wide roll after 2 min observation window.

mike: why did prefetch go so wild now? any recent change?

raj: investigating config churn. There was a rollout earlier today that increased prefetch concurrency (kv_prefetch.concurrency=8 -> 16) tied to a perf experiment. It passed perf tests but didn't account for extreme long prompt tails. experiment should have been gated by session length percentile.

emily: noted for postmortem. for now mitigation in place. updating status page: "Partial request failures in eu-west-1 due to runtime OOMs; mitigations applied; ongoing monitoring."

mike: support update: contacted top 5 affected customers with temporary workarounds (shorten history or pin model to smaller context). they acknowledged receipt.

raj: after rollout completes, propose next steps: 1) revert prefetch concurrency experiment 2) add guardrails on prefetch: max_prefetch_kv_tokens per-session 3) add alert for rapid per-process kv-cache growth (slope-based) 4) add chaos test for long-prompt tails in CI.

eng-runtime: agree. also add dynamic kill-switch for prefetch that auto-trips under memory pressure to avoid hand intervention.

sophie: final rollout done, region stable, OOMs dropped to baseline. enabling additional tracing to capture more sampling of long prompts for analysis.

oncall-sre: handing off to daytime oncall (maria) for post-incident follow-up. summary: root cause = prefetch concurrency + long prompt tail amplification + a batch config experiment. mitigation = disabled prefetch + reduced batch windows + canary rollout. customer impact = some request failures and notifications sent.

mike: will open incident PM ticket and assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml to own followups.

raj: pushing quick PR to gate prefetch experiment behind session-length check. PR: `github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4521`

emily: adding timeline + metrics to incident doc now.

oncall-sre: thanks everyone. feel free to continue thread for follow-ups. I'll close pager after 4h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
